methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.meta_description: Sources, scoring formula, anti-fraud rules and independence: how the charts are built.
methodology.heading: How :brand charts are built
methodology.intro: :brand ranks West African music from listening figures. Each week we measure how many times a song was played or viewed from Monday to Sunday, add these figures with a public formula, and publish the result on Tuesday.
methodology.sources_text: We read the public platform counters every day (YouTube, Audiomack, Boomplay and others depending on the country). When a platform does not share its data, we accept declarations from artists and labels, provided they can be cross-checked against public data.
methodology.score_text: Each audio stream is worth one point. Each view of an official video is worth half a point. We only count the growth of the week, not the total since release, so a new song can beat an old one.
methodology.diversity: To enter a country's Top :top, a song needs data from at least :sources sources. Otherwise it is capped just below.
methodology.ties: Ties are broken by number of sources, then biggest weekly growth, then last week's score.
methodology.upcoming: Announced change: formula v:version takes effect on :date.
methodology.country_rule: An artist is ranked in the country where they submit their music. The country where they are most played is shown separately on their page. Video, official audio, lyric and live versions of a song count together.
methodology.calendar: Tracking week: Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59, Lomé time. Computed on Monday, reviewed, published on Tuesday. Monthly charts come out on the first Tuesday of the following month.
methodology.checks_text: A song whose figures jump without explanation (more than :factor times its median of the last four weeks) is reviewed before publication. A declaration more than :tolerance% away from public data is checked. An abnormal ratio between views and likes triggers a review. Data that cannot be verified does not count. Songs removed for anomalies are listed below with the reason.
methodology.position_text: :brand is part of Novaluz Group, which includes the :label label. That label's artists carry a badge and follow exactly the same rules. Nobody at :brand can move a song by hand.
methodology.contest_text: Write to us with your evidence. We reply within seven days and every correction is published.
methodology.attribution: YouTube statistics obtained through the YouTube API Services. Spotify metadata (artwork, identifiers) used with no effect on the score.

submit.title: Submit figures
submit.intro: Some platforms do not publish their figures. Send a screenshot of your artist dashboard: it is reviewed, and counts only if it can be cross-checked against public data.
submit.step1: Take a screenshot of your artist dashboard (Spotify for Artists, Audiomack, Boomplay...) showing the period and the number of streams.
submit.step2: Fill in the form with the same figures.
submit.step3: Our team reviews the declaration before any computation. Inconsistent declarations are discarded.
submit.breakdown_hint: Country codes and percentages, for example: GH 60, NG 25, GB 15
submit.screenshot_hint: PNG, JPG or WebP, 5 MB max. It is never published.
submit.consent: I certify these figures are accurate and accept their verification. My details are only used for this follow-up.
submit.sent: Declaration received. It will be reviewed before being counted.
submit.error_period: Invalid period: past dates, end after start, three months at most.
submit.error_breakdown: Expected format: GH 60, NG 25 (100% total at most).

aside.label: Facts and news
aside.cta_text: Your Spotify for Artists, Audiomack or Boomplay figures can count. Send a screenshot and we will check it.
dyk.1: The cowrie, a small shell from the Indian Ocean, was used as currency in West Africa for centuries: what counts, what has value.
dyk.2: Only the week’s growth counts: a song released on Friday can beat a hit with millions of views built up over years.
dyk.3: A view of an official video is worth half a point, an audio stream a full point: deliberate listening weighs more.
dyk.4: To enter the Top 5, a song must be on at least two platforms: one source alone is not enough to dominate.
dyk.5: Video, official audio, lyric and live versions of the same song are added together: they count as one song.
dyk.6: An artist is ranked in the country where they submit their music, not by nationality. The country where they are most played appears on their page.
